[THOUGHT] 
This patient is an adult in home hospice with altered mental status who presents with fever (38.9°C), tachycardia, focal RUQ tenderness with a palpable RUQ mass, and an elevated WBC. RUQ ultrasound shows gallbladder wall thickening and pericholecystic fluid without gallstones and a normal-caliber common bile duct. These findings meet clinical and imaging criteria for acute cholecystitis, and the absence of gallstones in the setting of a critically ill or debilitated patient strongly favors acute acalculous cholecystitis. Alternative diagnoses (acute calculous cholecystitis) are less likely given no stones identified; ascending cholangitis is unlikely because there is no biliary dilation or reported cholestatic lab pattern/jaundice; hepatic abscess or perforation would typically have different imaging. Despite some missing/discrepant lab values, the constellation of fever, leukocytosis, RUQ signs, and ultrasound findings in this high-risk, debilitated patient is most consistent with acute acalculous cholecystitis.

[DIAGNOSIS]
Acute acalculous cholecystitis
